ui.longTermMemory.longtermmemorydetail.u: Under the Hood
Under the Hood
Long-Term Memory has two jobs. It writes durable facts from your sources, then reads the most useful facts back into the chat when they fit.
Writing to memory (Extraction)
Source notes.
The original source is kept as a source note. This gives every memory a place to point back to when you want to check where it came from.
Fingerprints.
Each source gets a fingerprint made from its content and source details. When the same source is seen again, that fingerprint helps the Engine tell what changed.
Candidate memories.
The extractor turns useful, lasting details into proposed memories. It leaves out passing actions, guesses, and details that are unlikely to matter later.
Evidence.
Every proposal keeps evidence showing which source supported it. Related facts can also point to the event that caused them.
Duplicate checks.
Near-duplicates are filtered out before review. One fact should not arrive as several slightly different proposals.
Review.
Nothing is written to the Vault automatically. Proposals wait in Review Queue, where you can accept, edit, or skip them.
Reading from memory (Recall)
Direct matches.
Direct matches look for known note IDs, source IDs, tags, and other metadata in your message.
Word matching.
Word matching checks which memory text shares useful terms with your message.
Keywords.
Keyword matching checks the compact keywords saved with each memory.
Related memories.
Graph matching follows links from strong matches to related memories.
Meaning.
Semantic matching compares meaning when an embedding index is available.

These lanes are fused into one ranking. A relevance threshold removes weak matches, and the token budget limits how much memory can enter the prompt. Higher-priority memories are kept first, and duplicate text is removed.
The Engine also cools down memories that were recently shown, so the same facts do not crowd out everything else. Sometimes that means a good match waits briefly before appearing again.
